newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Up to one million EU citizens take heroin.
newsitem.headline: Up to one million EU citizens take heroin.

text.p: Between 500,000 and one million European Union citizens take heroin, the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drugs Addiction said on Tuesday.
That means that between 0.25 percent and 0.50 percent of the total EU population takes the most problematic of drugs, the agency said, presenting its annual report.

But figures collected for drugs consumption and trafficking from one side of the 15-nation bloc to the other are little affected by whether a country liberalises drugs use or cracks down on it, the Lisbon-based centre said at a news conference.
"There's very little relation between the estimates of the number of addicts and the policy," said Georges Estievenart, director of the centre, set up in 1994 as part of the EU's fight against drugs.
Cannabis remains the most popular drug in the EU, with 10-20 percent of people between the ages of 18 to 35 having taken it at least once, it said.
While 10 percent have taken cannabis in Belgium, FInland and Sweden, more than 20 per cent have in France, Germany and Britain and 40 percent in Denmark.
Britain and the Nordic countries have witnessed a strong increase in the number of people taking amphetamines and synthetic "designer" drugs like ecstasy, it said.
Cocaine use is rare, but is still on the increase in most countries, the centre said, while smoking of the drug crack is emerging as a "significant problem" among urban marginalised groups.
